data.name: Constantino
data.gender_notes: Constantino is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'consanti' meaning 'constant'. This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including Constantine the Great, the first Christian Roman Emperor. The name Constantino carries the meaning “Firm and constant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Constantino usually hope their child will grow to embody firm and constant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of unwavering faith and devotion.
data.etymology: Constantino belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Firm and constant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Constantino total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: קונסטנטינו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קונסטנטינו הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בלטינית, ומשמעותו 'קבוע, נאמן'. השם נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'constans', שפירושה 'קבוע' או 'יציב'. השם קונסטנטינו היה שמו של מספר קיסרים רומיים, ביניהם קונסטנטין הגדול, שהיה קיסר רומי נוצרי חשוב במאה ה-4 לספירה. השם קונסטנטינו משמש עד היום כסמל לנאמנות וקביעות בקרב הנוצרים.

in_greek.name: Κωνσταντίνο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κωνσταντίνο προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Constantinus, που σημαίνει 'αμετάβλητος, σταθερός'. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν ιδιαίτερα δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ρώμη και συνδέεται με τον Κωνσταντίνο τον Μέγα, τον Ρωμαϊκό Αυτοκράτορα που εξάγαγε τον Χριστιανισμό ως επίσημη θρησκεία της Αυτοκρατορίας. Στην Εκκλησία και την παράδοση Χριστιανική, το όνομα Κωνσταντίνο συμβολίζει τη σταθερότητα και την αφοσίωση.

in_latin.name: Constantino
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Constantino origine Latina est, derivatum a verbo 'constans', quod significat 'constans' vel 'firmus'. Hoc nomen ad varios Imperatores Romanos, inter quos Constantinus Magnus, qui fuit Imperator Romanus et Christianus insignis saeculo IV p.C. Nomen Constantino in traditione Christiana persistit ut symbolum fidelitatis et constantiae.

in_english.name: Constantino
in_english.meaning: Constant and steadfast, a name symbolizing loyalty and faithfulness
in_english.long_meaning: The name Constantino is of Latin origin, derived from 'constans', meaning 'constant' or 'steadfast'. It is associated with several Roman Emperors, notably Constantine the Great, who played a pivotal role in establishing Christianity as a state religion. In Christian tradition, Constantino represents a commitment to faith and enduring loyalty. The name is popular across various Christian cultures for its historical significance and spiritual connotations.

data.cultural_impact: Constantino, as the name of the first Christian Roman Emperor, is deeply rooted in the history of Christianity as a symbol of the religion's rise to power and influence within the Roman Empire. This name carries a strong association with the golden age of Christianity, characterized by the spread of the faith throughout Europe and the establishment of Christian monarchies.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Constantino holds deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the strength, steadfastness, and unwavering commitment of the early Christian community to spread the Word of God. The name is a testament to the transformative power of faith, inspiring those who bear it to embody the steadfastness and unwavering commitment of Saint Constantine, the first Christian Roman Emperor.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Constantino: From the Latin name 'Constantinus', meaning 'steadfast, immovable'. In Christianity, St. Constantine the Great is remembered for his edict of Milan in AD 313, granting religious toleration to Christians in the Roman Empire. This name embodies the spiritual strength and unwavering faith of a steadfast believer.

historical_references.reference: Constantine the Great (272-337 AD) was a Roman emperor who converted the Roman Empire to Christianity.

trends: used as a given name for boys
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Constantino remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Constantino from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Constantino - "Firm and constant". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
